South Korea clears a 20-robot Robros industrial trial

The sandbox permits testing near workers with risk controls; it is not a completed factory-performance result.

Humanoids Daily ↗13 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Permission for real-site testing

Seoul Economic Daily reports that South Korea granted Robros a regulatory-sandbox exemption to trial 20 humanoids at manufacturing and logistics sites. This authorizes testing; it does not establish that all robots are deployed or have passed performance tests.

Four industrial settings

The named sites are Nepes, Sungwoo Hitech, HD Hyundai Samho and Delivery Lab. Planned tasks include cleaning semiconductor-packaging components, positioning vehicle body parts, stacking shipbuilding support components and moving refrigerated logistics containers.

Evidence for future safety standards

Work near people requires risk assessment and mitigation, with trial evidence intended to inform future standards. Robros’s separate AI roadmap for the first half of 2027 does not establish that the future model powers this trial or that these tasks already run autonomously.
